title: Left lifting classes are stable under transfinite compositions
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category [def-nagata-category] and $T$ a class of its morphisms. Say $a:A\to B$ belongs to ${}^{\square}T$ if every commutative square with left side $a$ and right side any $t:X\to Y$ in $T$ has a diagonal $h:B\to X$ with $ha=u$ and $th=v$, where $u:A\to X$ and $v:B\to Y$ are the horizontal maps. Let $\theta$ be any small ordinal and let $(Z_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\theta}$ be a coherent ordinal-indexed diagram in $\mathcal C$, continuous at every nonzero limit ordinal $\beta\leq\theta$: the canonical cocone from $(Z_\alpha)_{\alpha<\beta}$ to $Z_\beta$ is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. If every successor map $Z_\alpha\to Z_{\alpha+1}$ for $\alpha<\theta$ belongs to ${}^{\square}T$, then the composite $Z_0\to Z_\theta$ belongs to ${}^{\square}T$. Only the displayed colimits are required; no cocompleteness or smallness of $T$ is assumed.
